about: Free sound effects and background music for business videos, from GitHub repositories whose licence was checked file by file. Audio is not stored in this repo: scripts/get_sounds.py downloads only the folders listed here, at the pinned commit. 'license_check' is text that must appear in the licence file after download, or the download is refused.

sources.origin: All 320 sounds synthesised by code for this kit (no recordings). sounds.json describes each one.

sources.origin: Sound effects from Kenney and OpenGameArt CC0 packs plus sounds synthesised for the library; music from CC0 OpenGameArt collections, except music/corporate (Sascha Ende, CC BY 4.0). Loudness-normalised. Sources listed in CREDITS.md.
sources.notes: Each music track has a .json beside it with its beat map (bpm, cue points); index.json has mood, tags, length and loudness for every file.

sources.origin: Synthesised from code (no samples), made for content creators; nine short background beds for explainers and vlogs.
Kenney's Interface Sounds 1.0 (kenney.nl), unchanged: 100 clicks, switches, confirmations, errors, glass and glitches.
Kenney's UI Audio, Interface Sounds, Digital Audio, Sci-Fi Sounds and Impact Sounds packs; each pack's original licence kept in credits/.

sources.license: CC0-1.0 (only the Kenney folders listed; this repo's assets/wow folder is Blizzard's and is never downloaded)
sources.origin: Kenney's Music Jingles (short pizzicato and hit stings) and Digital Audio packs, as published in soundcn.
AtomCut's seed packs, synthesised from DSP: motion-graphics hits, UI clicks, impacts and risers.

sources.license: CC0-1.0 (stated in the repo's SFX skill; the code is MIT)
sources.origin: 17 sound effects for UI and video (whoosh, swoosh, riser, boom, shutter, success, notification). The repo states CC0 but doesn't name where the sounds came from: prefer the sources above when one fits.

credit.corpora/oculus-audio-pack/: "Oculus Audio Pack 01" by Oculus VR, LLC (https://developers.meta.com/vr/downloads/package/oculus-audio-pack-1/), licensed under CC BY 4.0. Files renamed to the UCS naming convention; OGG previews transcoded from the original WAVs.

sources.origin: Professional sound effects released by Oculus (Meta), named with the UCS convention. Only the UI, whoosh, design and musical-sting sets are listed here.
13 instrumental tracks (ambient and cinematic) released as CC0 by AERIS MUSIC. A new, small publisher: listen before using it in an ad.

rejected.why: About 40 GB scraped from several sites, including Pixabay, whose licence is not CC0. Track licences can't be verified one by one.
The code is MIT, but no licence is stated for the sounds themselves.

CC BY 4.0, but many tracks are arrangements of copyrighted game music (Final Fantasy, Castlevania), and the originals are fantasy and game moods, not business.
CC0, but instrument samples for making music, not sound effects for videos.
